mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 600k signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% interacts with a concurrent decline in personal income growth (PAYEMS) to signal restrictive monetary policy coincident with weakening income dynamics, which together produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with income deceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month, combined with a concurrent drop in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals a sudden labor market shock that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS falls YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index above 4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which is expected to persistently raise interest rates and reduce equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
